steps.what: Inspect work progress equipment and sites against safety requirements and specifications
Judge compliance and direct correction or stop unsafe work

tasks.design: Keep direct inspection and corrective decisions with the supervisor. {DOCS} can hold the issued requirements, but a checklist or photograph does not replace examining actual site conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safety and compliance require contextual physical inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital reference material does not establish a replacement for direct observations.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden defects and changing conditions during active work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when apparently normal work needs immediate intervention.
tasks.altitude: No change to inspection authority or site responsibility.

reach.task: Investigate specification issues needing specialist assessment

evidence.claim: The proposed workflow retains inspection and safety decisions and claims no software labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is inspection and immediate direction; report preparation is a separate task and earns no saving here.
s1 produces the observations used in s2; no structured safety flag or automated image judgement is assumed.
Issued specifications and requirements are unchanged upstream documents, not new capture demanded from others.
No new system or ongoing upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Inspection scope, site risks and local authority limits
research_questions: Is duplicate report entry separately measurable without reducing physical inspection?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=70+30=100. Direct inspection and judgement retain full time and no new upkeep is proposed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read specifications and plan construction procedures

steps.what: Find issued specifications and blueprints for the relevant construction work
Read specifications and blueprints to determine requirements and plan construction procedures

tasks.design: Configure indexed work-package views and revision filters in {DOCS} to locate issued drawings and specifications. The supervisor confirms the selected versions and reads the complete relevant material to determine requirements and procedures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right issued documents can be separate from interpreting them.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and search can narrow retrieval without generating a technical interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicts between drawings, specifications and actual conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding which details change the construction method.
tasks.altitude: Less document hunting; technical interpretation and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve inconsistent drawing and specification requirements
reach.learn: How to identify exact revision and clause references

evidence.claim: Indexed document retrieval can reduce locating time without replacing blueprint interpretation; this is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary includes retrieval and interpretation only, excluding authoring and approving designs.
Existing document controllers produce document ID, work package, discipline, revision, issue status and file during unchanged document issue; no new tagging burden is assumed for free.
s1 includes supervisor selection and revision checks. Missing metadata triggers manual register lookup; unfamiliar content still receives full reading in s2.
Test native filters and search before custom code. If required metadata does not already exist, measure its production before deployment.
Existing document software runtime earns no saving; recurring local view and metadata corrections have an allowance.
unknowns: Document metadata quality and actual retrieval share
research_questions: Do current issue metadata and native filters reduce retrieval time after revision checks?

already_counted.description: Confirm document scope and revisions in s1

incremental.description: Maintain local document views and report metadata faults

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=8+80=88; gross 12 minus 1 focal upkeep gives net 11. High needs existing accurate metadata and substantial searching; low covers manual register fallback. Document-controller upkeep is separate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise coordinate and schedule construction workers

steps.what: Gather worker availability material readiness and work dependencies
Prepare construction activity schedule from checked constraints
Check schedule and coordinate and supervise workers as site conditions change

tasks.design: Configure an editable scheduling board in {PROJECT} before adding a separate scheduling service. Reuse checked constraints to reduce schedule rewriting while the supervisor decides the sequence, checks coverage and leads the crew.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedule edits require repetitive formatting and copying alongside live coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Native planning boards support reusable work items and visible conflicts.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected conditions and practical coordination between trades.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which nominally possible sequence is workable and safe on site.
tasks.altitude: Less schedule maintenance; supervision and live coordination stay central.

reach.task: Connect short-term site constraints to project milestones
reach.learn: How dependencies affect the wider programme

evidence.claim: Exact for Bouw supports staff, subcontractor and equipment planning; this supports testing native planning software, not the estimated saving.
The time split and reduction in schedule rewriting are model assumptions.

assumptions: Boundary is activity scheduling and live coordination; task-specific employee assignment is allocated separately rather than added twice.
The supervisor produces job ID, date/shift, availability, material readiness, dependency and equipment constraints in s1; all calls and capture remain counted there.
s2 includes board entry, manual sequencing and corrections; no ready-made structured constraint feed or model worker ranking is assumed.
Test existing planning-board configuration first. Missing information requires the existing calls and manual edits, not a fabricated availability flag.
The supervisor retains all safety decisions, schedule checks and crew interaction in s3; local consultation and access need confirmation.
unknowns: Existing planning tools, repeated schedule entry and workforce consultation requirements
research_questions: Does the native board save rewriting time after entering current constraints?

already_counted.description: Constraint capture in s1 and schedule editing in s2 remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain board templates and resolve stale work items

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+12+60=92; gross 8 minus 1 upkeep gives net 7. High needs repetitive schedule rewriting; low covers frequent changes and manual capture absorbing the benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess specific job material requirements and available workers
Assign work to employees and explain requirements and limitations

tasks.design: Retain individual work assignment and the associated briefing with the supervisor. {PROJECT} may display an existing schedule, but that does not replace deciding whether a particular worker can undertake the job under actual conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments depend on contextual competence, materials and site readiness.
tasks.enabler_now: A planning display can support awareness without granting new assignment authority.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing competence, safe working and changing materials.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertainty and explaining a job so workers can raise concerns.
tasks.altitude: No change to employee assignment authority.

reach.task: Clarify worker competence and support needs for a specific job

evidence.claim: This design retains person-specific assignment and briefing rather than assuming performance-based automated allocation.

assumptions: Boundary is individual assignment judgement and briefing; the activity scheduling task must not be added again for the same action.
s1 counts direct assessment of job requirements, materials and worker suitability. No structured competence or readiness flag is invented.
s2 retains the actual decision and employee conversation; existing upstream schedule capture is unchanged.
No additional system, employee scoring or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Local assignment authority and competence assessment practices
research_questions: Is any repeated assignment recording separately measurable from necessary assessment and briefing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100. Assessment, assignment and briefing retain their time with no additional upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce document hunting and schedule rewriting while retaining site leadership.
reach: Connect site constraints with planning and design roles
role.ambitious_version: Lead site work with dependable references and less repeated schedule maintenance.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
